A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same VGA research. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices are readable, allowing relocated and renumbered material to be matched reliably.

before.justification: V1 reports original POPE, CHAIR, and AMBER experiments, visual-grounding analyses, ablations, hyperparameter studies, and latency measurements.

after.justification: V2 retains these original experiments and adds MME results, grounding-reliability analyses, a first-token approximation comparison, and output-token latency measurements.

M1.justification: VSC/VSS grounding, additive attention guidance, head balancing, programmed grounding updates, and the first-token approximation remain unchanged. Appendix G tests an alternative token aggregation but retains the original procedure. Notation corrections and removal of the standard self-attention formula do not establish an algorithm change.

E1.justification: V2 Appendix F adds evaluation on MME perception tasks, extending coverage beyond the original hallucination benchmarks. AMBER attribute and relation tasks already appeared in v1; their separate scores in v2 Table 8 are additional reporting, not newly introduced task coverage.

E2.justification: Matched benchmark comparisons retain Vanilla, PAI, PAICD, VAF, and TARAC. The LLaVA-13B AMBER comparison moves from v1 Table 3 to v2 Table 5 without losing comparators. New Table 8 uses existing comparators Vanilla and TARAC, introducing no new comparison method.

E3.justification: V2 adds protocols for selecting positive examples with DICE below 0.01, defining high-semantic regions using above-mean VSS, and matching true-negative counts to false-positive counts for correlation analysis. It also adds TPOT measurement on CHAIR. These extend evaluation without establishing changes to the retained benchmark settings.

E4.justification: Section 5.4 substantially extends the grounding analysis with quantitative negative-sample diagnostics, performance under low-Dice grounding, and true-positive versus false-negative failure analysis. Appendix G additionally compares first-token confidence with all-token aggregation. These examine previously untested reliability and approximation questions; the original ablations remain.

E5.justification: V2 adds a Pearson correlation reported as 0.414 ± 0.019 after count-matched negative sampling, but does not define the uncertainty term or repetition count. It also removes v1 Appendix D's statement that TTFT was averaged over three runs. Neither change establishes an increase in experimental runs.

E6.justification: Matched original benchmark and ablation scores are unchanged, but substantive new findings are reported: low-Dice grounding achieves 88.5% accuracy versus 87.1% with uniform guidance; Table 8 adds AMBER task-specific and MME scores; and TPOT overhead is 6.01%. V2 also adds grounding/error statistics and a negligible-difference token-aggregation finding, while omitting the original absolute TTFT timings.

T1.justification: Section 5.4.1 introduces the Informative Coefficient, defined as normalized VSC mass over regions with above-mean VSS. This is a new mathematical diagnostic definition. The core VGA derivations remain equivalent, and no new theorem or proof is introduced.

C1.justification: V2 modestly qualifies the efficiency headline: it removes v1's general 'just 4.36%' latency-overhead claim from the abstract and contributions, retaining 4.36% specifically for TTFT alongside 6.01% TPOT overhead. The central claims of training-free, single-pass, FlashAttention-compatible hallucination mitigation remain.

C2.justification: V2 adds substantive explanations and boundaries for grounding reliability. Section 5.4.2 attributes useful but spatially inaccurate grounding to information carried from preceding visual tokens, and identifies degraded feature extraction as a failure condition. Appendices F–G additionally explain broader applicability and the first-token approximation, extending v1's emphasis on accurate grounding.

D1.justification: V2 newly explains that the VSC threshold was selected by F1-maximizing grid search on COCO Random, and clarifies the guidance-strength symbol as beta in the appendix. Conversely, it removes the TTFT sample count of 1,000 and absolute timings. Hardware, decoding settings, and code access remain documented; these disclosure changes do not establish altered original experiments.

R1.justification: V2 adds references for MME, GQA, A-OKVQA, and MLLMs Know Where to Look. The latter replaces the source cited for layer-14 attention extraction in Figure 5. Related-work positioning is otherwise largely retained, with a revised emphasis on an internally derived visual prior.

P1.justification: The experimental narrative is substantially reorganized: model descriptions and detailed results discussion move into the appendix, main setup/results prose is condensed, and the captioning and perception analyses are reordered and regrouped. Introduction and method explanations are also revised, alongside affiliation updates and new acknowledgments.

P2.justification: Figure 1 gains patch numbering and tokenization labels, and several captions are clarified. The LLaVA-13B block is split from Table 3 into appendix Table 5, Table 8 is added, and existing figures and tables are relocated or renumbered. Most existing graphical content and table designs remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: V2 improves scrutiny of the existing method through grounding-failure analysis, a first-token approximation check, MME evaluation, and decoding-latency measurement. These provide useful support and clearer applicability boundaries while retaining the original benchmark evidence. The gain is limited by sparse details for some new analyses and the removal of TTFT sample/run counts and absolute timings.
